entries.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
entries.description: The built-in engine. 25 European languages, punctuation + casing, word timestamps; the only model with a Qualcomm NPU path.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: docs/benchmarks.md 5.1 - `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --backend cpu`, 12 FLEURS clips, 2026-08-27

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: docs/benchmarks.md 5.1 - `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --backend npu`, encoder on Hexagon HTP V81, 12 FLEURS clips, 2026-08-26

entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine (Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E94100): end-to-end RTF 0.032 on the CPU EP and 0.0145 with the encoder on the Hexagon HTP V81, word-weighted WER 5.4% / 4.8% over 12 FLEURS clips - see docs/benchmarks.md 5.1. The per-language wer_estimates come from the same run with only 3 clips per language, so treat them as indicative, not statistically meaningful; the English figure is dominated by FLEURS number-word and casing normalisation ('2' vs 'two'), not misrecognition. download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact pinned file sizes in models/manifests/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.json and cover the CPU int8 artifact set, which is the only hash-pinned target today. The NPU path additionally needs a static-shape encoder and builds a ~1.2 GB HTP context binary locally on first use (~106 s, cached thereafter) - that is generated on the machine, not downloaded, and is not counted in disk_bytes. GPU: the same file also runs on a GPU through ONNX Runtime's WebGPU provider - no separate artifact and no extra download - measured on the X2's integrated Adreno at RTF 0.0862, WER 4.8% over the same 12 clips. The hardware field below lists artifact targets (which pinned file sets exist), not every provider that can run them.

entries.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: English-only sibling of the built-in v3, driven through sherpa-onnx as an offline transducer. Punctuation + casing; CPU only here.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the four pinned file sizes in models/manifests/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-en.json (encoder/decoder/joiner int8 + tokens.txt); disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. Every SHA-256 in that manifest was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksums for these files anywhere. The licence is cc-by-4.0 as declared in the export repository's own model card. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-int8.tar.bz2, and LocalWisper's downloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. NOT VERIFIED: nothing here has been run on any machine - no RTF, no WER, no measurements. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL: they match the v3 entry because this is the same architecture and parameter count, not because this export was benchmarked. wer_estimates is deliberately empty: NVIDIA publishes v2 figures for its own NeMo checkpoint, not for this int8 ONNX export, and quantization moves WER. Distinct from parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3: v2 is English-only and runs through the sherpa engine feature, so it has no NPU artifact and no Qualcomm path. The engine string is deliberately `nemo_transducer`, not `parakeet_tdt`: the built-in parakeet_tdt engine expects the istupakov file layout (nemo128.onnx + vocab.txt + a fused decoder_joint graph) and cannot load this sherpa-style encoder/decoder/joiner triple, so labelling it parakeet_tdt would promise a path that does not exist.

entries.name: SenseVoice Small (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Alibaba's non-autoregressive multilingual model: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese in one pass, with inverse text normalisation and punctuation.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the two pinned file sizes in models/manifests/sense-voice-small.json (model.int8.onnx + tokens.txt); both SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes, because upstream publishes none. SOURCE: the `asr-models` GitHub release only ships .tar.bz2 archives, which the installer cannot unpack, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE - READ THIS: not an SPDX licence. The export repository's LICENSE file points at the FunASR Model Open Source License Agreement v1.1 (https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR/blob/main/MODEL_LICENSE), a custom Alibaba Group agreement which permits use, copying, modification and sharing but requires attribution and retention of model names, disclaims all liability, and terminates if you 'denigrate' the software. It is not OSI-approved and is more restrictive than the MIT/CC-BY terms of the other entries; check it before redistributing. NOT VERIFIED: no run of any kind on any machine, so no measurements. wer_estimates is empty: FunAudioLLM publishes comparisons against Whisper on AISHELL-1/Common Voice for the full-precision checkpoint, not for this int8 ONNX export, and we did not retrieve that table. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; 'very_fast' reflects that SenseVoice Small is non-autoregressive (one encoder pass, no token-by-token decode loop), not a timing. The engine string is `sense_voice`, which this build's EngineKind does not know - it round-trips as an unknown engine, which is intended for a catalog that may outlive the binary.

entries.name: Whisper tiny.en (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: English-only 39M-parameter Whisper. The smallest useful fallback; int8 encoder/decoder ONNX.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the three pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-tiny-en.json (tiny.en-encoder.int8.onnx, tiny.en-decoder.int8.onnx, tiny.en-tokens.txt); all three SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes - upstream publishes none. The 39M parameter count is from the official openai/whisper README. SOURCE CHANGED from the earlier entry: it used to point at sherpa-onnx-whisper-tiny.en.tar.bz2 (118071777 bytes) in the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release, but the installer cannot unpack archives, so the manifest now pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. Only the int8 variants are pinned; the fp32 pair exists in the same repository and would add about 150 MB for a quality difference we have not measured. NOT VERIFIED: nothing here has been run on any machine. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL and the RTF shown by `lw models list` is an estimate. wer_estimates is empty: the openai/whisper README publishes no per-size WER table, and quantization would move it anyway. Needs the not-yet-default `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Whisper base (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Multilingual 74M-parameter Whisper. Covers 99 languages at modest accuracy; a reasonable CPU-only fallback where Parakeet has no language coverage.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the three pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-base.json (base-encoder.int8.onnx, base-decoder.int8.onnx, base-tokens.txt); all three SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes - upstream publishes none. The 74M parameter count and the 99-language list are taken from the official openai/whisper README and whisper/tokenizer.py LANGUAGES, minus 'yue' (Cantonese), which that table only wires up for large-v3. SOURCE CHANGED from the earlier entry: it used to point at sherpa-onnx-whisper-base.tar.bz2 (207557382 bytes) in the `asr-models` GitHub release, but the installer cannot unpack archives, so the manifest now pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. Only the int8 variants are pinned; the fp32 pair in the same repository would add about 130 MB. NOT VERIFIED: nothing here has been run on any machine. Whisper accuracy varies enormously by language and the openai/whisper README publishes per-size WER for no size at all, so wer_estimates is deliberately empty rather than filled with plausible-looking numbers. Quality/speed tiers are editorial; the RTF shown is an estimate, never measured here. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Whisper small (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Multilingual 244M-parameter Whisper. The accuracy step up from base, at roughly 3x the compute; still CPU-only here.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the three pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-small.json (small-encoder.int8.onnx, small-decoder.int8.onnx, small-tokens.txt); all three SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes - upstream publishes none. The 244M parameter count and the 99-language list come from openai/whisper (tokenizer.py LANGUAGES minus 'yue', which is large-v3 only). SOURCE CHANGED from the earlier entry: it used to point at sherpa-onnx-whisper-small.tar.bz2 (639387718 bytes) in the `asr-models` GitHub release, but the installer cannot unpack archives, so the manifest now pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. Only the int8 variants are pinned, which is why the download is 375 MB rather than the ~970 MB the fp32 pair would cost. NOT VERIFIED: nothing here has been run on any machine, and no WER is pinned. The openai/whisper README's relative-speed column puts small at roughly 4x realtime versus tiny at 10x, which is why the speed tier drops two steps - that ordering is published, the RTF number this CLI shows is still only an estimate. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Whisper medium (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Multilingual 769M-parameter Whisper. The accuracy end of the classic Whisper ladder, and the first entry here that is slower than real time on a laptop CPU.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/whisper-medium`, 2026-09-16, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.054 and mean RTF 1.2499 over 12 clip(s) in en/es/ru/uk - the whole tests/fixtures/audio set, 3 FLEURS clips per language, about 82 s of audio. 12 clips is indicative, not statistically meaningful, and this figure must not be compared with the 3-clip English figures carried by the English-only entries in this catalog.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-medium.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16: see the measurement below and read its source line before quoting either number. That run is the only accuracy figure this entry carries - wer_estimates is deliberately empty, because OpenAI publishes no per-size WER table and any number it did publish would describe the full-precision checkpoint, not this int8 export. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL: 'slow' is at least consistent with the measured RTF of 1.25 (slower than real time), and 'best' places medium above whisper-small on family ordering, which a 12-clip run is far too small to prove on its own. The 769M parameter count and the 99-language list come from openai/whisper (README, and tokenizer.py LANGUAGES minus 'yue', which is wired up only for large-v3). Only the int8 encoder/decoder pair is pinned; the full-precision graphs sit in the same upstream repository and would cost several times the download for a quality difference nobody here has measured. LICENCE NOTE: recorded as MIT, the licence of the openai/whisper repository whose original checkpoints sherpa-onnx's export script downloads and converts; the `openai/whisper-*` model cards on Hugging Face declare apache-2.0 instead, so read both before redistributing. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Whisper large-v3-turbo (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: OpenAI's large-v3 encoder with a 4-layer decoder: the lowest WER measured on this project's 12-clip fixture set, at about a third of medium's cost.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/whisper-turbo`, 2026-09-16, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.042 and mean RTF 0.4690 over 12 clip(s) in en/es/ru/uk - the whole tests/fixtures/audio set, 3 FLEURS clips per language, about 82 s of audio. 12 clips is indicative, not statistically meaningful, and this figure must not be compared with the 3-clip English figures carried by the English-only entries in this catalog.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-turbo.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16: WER 0.042 over the same 12 clips on which whisper-medium scored 0.054 and parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 scored 0.054, at RTF 0.469 against medium's 1.250. On this fixture set that is the best accuracy-per-second of any Whisper entry here, but 12 clips cannot settle an ordering - read the source line before quoting it. wer_estimates stays empty for the usual reason: OpenAI's published figures describe the full-precision checkpoint, not this int8 export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL. WHAT TURBO IS: large-v3's encoder with the decoder cut from 32 layers to 4 - not a smaller, weaker large, but large-v3's acoustic model with a cheap decoder; OpenAI documents it as degrading on some languages relative to large-v3 itself. The language list is therefore large-v3's: openai/whisper tokenizer.py LANGUAGES plus 'yue', which large-v3 is the first size to support and which turbo inherits with the same tokenizer. Only the int8 encoder/decoder pair is pinned; the full-precision graphs sit in the same upstream repository and would cost several times the download for a quality difference nobody here has measured. LICENCE NOTE: recorded as MIT, the licence of the openai/whisper repository whose original checkpoints sherpa-onnx's export script downloads and converts; the `openai/whisper-*` model cards on Hugging Face declare apache-2.0 instead, so read both before redistributing. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Distil-Whisper small.en (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Hugging Face's distilled English-only Whisper: 2 decoder layers instead of 12, so it decodes an order of magnitude faster than whisper-small.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/whisper-distil-small-en`, 2026-09-16, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.062 and mean RTF 0.0751 over 3 clip(s) in en. Run against the full 12-clip tests/fixtures/audio set: bench transcribed and timed all twelve but scored only the three English clips, because this export claims English alone and a WER against the es/ru/uk clips would describe nothing. Mean RTF over all 12 clips, scored or not, was 0.0805. A 3-clip English figure is NOT comparable with the 12-clip multilingual figures on whisper-medium and whisper-turbo.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-distil-small-en.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE: MIT, as declared by the upstream model card of distil-whisper/distil-small.en (Hugging Face); its teacher, OpenAI Whisper small.en, is MIT in the openai/whisper repository too, so unlike the plain Whisper entries there is no apache-2.0/MIT disagreement to warn about here. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16 - see the measurement below and read its source line. wer_estimates is empty: the Distil-Whisper paper publishes WER for its own full-precision checkpoints on LibriSpeech and out-of-distribution sets, which is neither this int8 export nor this fixture set. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; that 'fast' lands on the measured RTF of 0.075 almost exactly is luck, not method. WHAT DISTIL IS: the same encoder as Whisper small.en with the decoder distilled from 12 layers to 2, which is why it is a third of whisper-small's download and roughly ten times quicker here. Still English-only: the benchmark did transcribe the Russian clips with it, and what came out was not Russian. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Moonshine tiny en (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: English-only ASR designed for short utterances on small devices; int8 ONNX, no fixed 30 s padding, so cost scales with the length of what you actually said.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/moonshine-tiny-en`, 2026-09-16, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.092 and mean RTF 0.0125 over 3 clip(s) in en. bench transcribed and timed all 12 fixture clips but scored only the three English ones, because Moonshine claims English alone; mean RTF over all 12, scored or not, was 0.0119. REPLACES an earlier single-clip point (rtf 0.038, wer 0.200 on fleurs_en_1.wav alone) taken through the lw-engine-sherpa integration test before lw-cli had a sherpa feature: same model, same machine, a third of the data. Three clips and 63 reference words is still indicative rather than statistically meaningful, and is NOT comparable with the 12-clip multilingual figures on parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3, whisper-medium or whisper-turbo.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the five pinned file sizes in models/manifests/moonshine-tiny-en.json (preprocess.onnx plus the int8 encode / uncached_decode / cached_decode graphs and tokens.txt); all five SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes - upstream publishes none. The MIT licence is the LICENSE file committed in the export repository (Copyright (c) 2024 Useful Sensors). SOURCE CHANGED from the earlier entry: it used to point at sherpa-onnx-moonshine-tiny-en-int8.tar.bz2 (107600538 bytes) in the `asr-models` GitHub release, but the installer cannot unpack archives, so the manifest now pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. preprocess.onnx is full precision upstream and is pinned as a common file because there is no int8 variant of it. INSTALLED AND RUN, 2026-09-16: it was installed with `lw models install moonshine-tiny-en`, which downloaded all five files and SHA-256-verified each against the committed manifest, and then benchmarked over the whole committed fixture set - see the measurement below and read its source line before quoting either number. That measurement REPLACED an earlier one-clip point (wer 0.200 on fleurs_en_1.wav alone); one measurement per model and hardware, taken the same way as every other entry here, is worth more than two that disagree because one used a third of the data. NOT VERIFIED: three English clips is a small sample, so wer_estimates is still empty; Moonshine publishes WER comparisons against Whisper tiny/base for its own checkpoints, not for this int8 ONNX export, so nothing is quoted from upstream either. The quality and speed tiers remain EDITORIAL. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Moonshine base en (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: The larger English-only Moonshine. Same variable-length design as tiny, roughly 2.3x the download, for better accuracy on harder audio.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the five pinned file sizes in models/manifests/moonshine-base-en.json (preprocess.onnx plus the int8 encode / uncached_decode / cached_decode graphs and tokens.txt); all five SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes - upstream publishes none. The MIT licence is the LICENSE file committed in the export repository (Copyright (c) 2024 Useful Sensors). SOURCE: the `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as sherpa-onnx-moonshine-base-en-int8.tar.bz2, which the installer cannot unpack, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. NOT VERIFIED: nothing here has been run on any machine. wer_estimates is empty for the same reason as the tiny entry - the published Moonshine comparisons are for the upstream checkpoints, not this int8 export. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL: 'better' places base above Moonshine tiny and Whisper base on the strength of its file sizes and the family's own ordering, not on any measurement taken here; 'fast' rather than 'very_fast' for the same reason. entries.name: Paraformer-large zh (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Alibaba DAMO Academy's non-autoregressive Chinese ASR: one encoder pass, no token-by-token decode, so it is effectively instant on a laptop CPU.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/paraformer-zh`, 2026-09-16, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.277 and mean RTF 0.0109 over 3 clip(s) in en. READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE WER: this is a Chinese-first export and tests/fixtures/audio contains no Chinese at all, so the only clips it could be scored on are the three English ones - a secondary ability, not the job it was built for. The number is real and was produced by this model on this machine; it is simply not a measurement of Chinese accuracy, and no measurement of Chinese accuracy exists in this catalog. Mean RTF over all 12 clips, scored or not, was 0.0101.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/paraformer-zh.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE: Apache-2.0, as declared in the `License` field of the upstream ModelScope model page iic/speech_paraformer-large_asr_nat-zh-cn-16k-common-vocab8358-tensorflow1, which the sherpa-onnx export README names as its source. Note that this is a *different* licence from the other Alibaba entry in this catalog: sense-voice-small carries the custom, non-SPDX FunASR Model Open Source License Agreement 1.1. Neither the sherpa-onnx export repository nor the ModelScope repository ships a LICENSE file next to the weights, so the ModelScope metadata field is the whole of the evidence - check it yourself before redistributing. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16, and the source line of that measurement matters more than the number: the fixtures cannot reach this model's actual language. wer_estimates is empty - FunASR publishes AISHELL/WenetSpeech figures for the full-precision checkpoint, not for this int8 ONNX export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL: 'very_fast' reflects the architecture (non-autoregressive, one encoder pass) and is corroborated by the measured RTF of 0.011; 'better' is a family ranking, not a result. Languages are listed as zh and en because the vocab8358 'common' model does carry English tokens and demonstrably produced English output in the run above - Chinese is what it is for. The engine string is `paraformer`, which this build's EngineKind does not know - it round-trips as an unknown engine, exactly as `sense_voice` does, which is intended for a catalog that may outlive the binary. lw-engine-sherpa does recognize the layout: a lone model.onnx plus tokens.txt is ambiguous between SenseVoice and Paraformer, and the detector breaks the tie on the directory name, so the manifest's local_dir deliberately contains the word `paraformer` and must keep it. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Zipformer ru (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: A 70 MB Russian-only Zipformer transducer from the Vosk project. The smallest and fastest strong Russian option in this catalog.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench <ru-only copy of tests/fixtures/audio> --model-dir <models>/zipformer-ru`, 2026-09-16, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.000 and mean RTF 0.0089 over 3 clip(s) in ru. THREE clips and 33 reference words: a zero here means 'no word errors on 20 seconds of clean FLEURS read speech after the benchmark's lowercase/punctuation normalisation', not 'this model does not make mistakes'. Do not compare it with the 12-clip multilingual figures on whisper-medium / whisper-turbo, which cover four languages and four times the audio.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/zipformer-ru.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE: Apache-2.0, declared on the upstream model page alphacep/vosk-model-ru, which the sherpa-onnx export README names as its source. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16 - read the measurement's source line, which explains both the three-clip sample and the language subset, before quoting the zero. WHY A LANGUAGE SUBSET: `lw bench` scores only the clips in languages the engine claims, but lw-engine-sherpa reports a whole-family language list for offline transducers (the 25 European languages of the multilingual NeMo releases), which this monolingual export does not speak. Left to the full 12-clip set it would have been scored against English, Spanish and Ukrainian as well, producing a WER that describes nothing. So the run used a copy of tests/fixtures/audio holding only the Russian clips and their fixtures.json entries; the audio and the reference transcripts are the repository's own, unmodified. WHY IT IS HERE: the Russian coverage in this catalog was previously Whisper (multilingual, slow) or parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 (640 MB). This is 70 MB, runs at RTF 0.009, and made no errors on the Russian fixtures - by some distance the cheapest Russian dictation option here. It emits lowercase text with no punctuation, which Whisper and Parakeet do not. wer_estimates is empty: Alpha Cephei publishes numbers for its own full-precision Vosk packaging, not for this int8 ONNX export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; 'better' rather than 'best' keeps a 70 MB model below the 240 MB GigaAM v2 entry, which the three-clip run cannot separate from it. The engine string is `nemo_transducer`, as on parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-en. In this catalog that string means 'the sherpa-onnx offline transducer loader' - the encoder/decoder/joiner/tokens.txt layout - not a claim about who trained the weights. It is deliberately not `parakeet_tdt`: the built-in parakeet_tdt engine only loads the istupakov file layout (nemo128.onnx + vocab.txt + a fused decoder_joint graph) and cannot read this triple, so labelling it parakeet_tdt would promise a path that does not exist. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.
